# A downstream node hears when held work rolls back

When a co-holder fails, the claim is abandoned and the acquirer emits
`terminal/error/abandoned`. Subscribers learn of the rollback at the moment it
happens — by naming that signal, or through the ordinary error-family pattern.

## The template

```yaml
name: held-abandon-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: acquirer
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: data
        intent: rw
        alias: ds
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          v: {type: integer, default: 1}

  - type: co-holder
    executor: verifier-http
    holds:
      ds: {from: acquirer}
    subscribes:
      - node: acquirer
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    error_types:
      "verifier/network_error": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url: {type: string, default: "http://127.0.0.1:9/refused"}

  - type: watcher-exact
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: acquirer
        type: terminal/error/abandoned
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}

  - type: watcher-family
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: acquirer
        type: terminal/error/*
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}

  - type: watcher-success
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: acquirer
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}
```

The three watchers are outside the holding subgraph. The co-holder calls an
address nothing is listening on, so its work fails.

## What the product does

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

The failure rolls the claim back with a single `claim_resolution.abandon`. The
acquirer emits exactly one terminal signal: `terminal/error/abandoned`.

`watcher-exact` runs, its `work_started` at a sequence number after the abandon.
It learns of the rollback at the moment the held work was abandoned, not later.

`watcher-family` runs too, on the same rollback and at the same moment. A
template author who already catches every error of an upstream does not need a
separate subscription to learn that held work was rolled back.

`watcher-success` never runs. A rollback is never reported downstream as a
success.
